The paper investigates the scattering from impedance strips and impedance-loaded conducting strips.
The impedance strips are analyzed using Senior's impedance half plane formulation.
The scattering from impedance-loaded strips is analyzed using Maliuzhinets' impedance wedge formulation.
The multiple diffractions on both types of strips are developed using the Extended Spectral Ray Method.

Sample calculations are made for impedance strips and impedance-loaded strips for a large purely capacitive impedance, a large purely inductive impedance, a large real impedance, and a small real impedance.
Measurements are made for impedance strips and impedance loaded strips and are used to compare against predictions.
The impedance materials used are two magnetic radar absorbing materials (SF 10 and FG 40) and two resistive materials (SC 100 and VF 10).
The paper develops computational subroutines to calculate the 2D edge diffraction of impedance edges and junctions.
The computational methods are accurate for electrically large targets and computationally efficient compared to the method of moments technique.
The paper presents a summary and conclusions, as well as recommendations for further research.
The objectives of the thesis are to develop computational methods, use them to predict scattering patterns, and verify the accuracy against measurements.
The paper investigates the scattering characteristics of purely inductive, purely capacitive, large non-reactive, and small non-reactive impedance strips and impedance loaded strips.
The paper uses the impedance half plane and impedance wedge formulations to develop the primary diffraction mechanisms.
The Extended Spectral Ray Method is used to develop the secondary diffraction mechanisms on impedance strips and impedance double wedges.
The paper compares the scattering predictions against measurements made on physical samples using the impedance materials.
